name: Yago Mann
photo_alt: Yago Mann sitting on graffiti-covered steps
bio: Yago has spent his career helping artists sound more like themselves. First as a guitar player on other people’s records, and now as a producer, his work is built around drawing out the version of the song you’ve been chasing – not imposing his own sound on top of it.
He hears performance before he hears production, which means the take you love but keep second-guessing is often the one he’ll fight for.
The sound he gravitates toward is what he calls “melancholy with momentum”: sweet vocals over distorted textures, drums that hit before you’ve decided to move, bittersweet without becoming heavy.
You won’t leave a session sounding more like Yago. You’ll leave sounding more like yourself – with someone who never made it about him.

questions.q: What’s a record that changed how you hear music?
questions.a: Def Leppard’s Hysteria, The Beatles’ Abbey Road, Pink Floyd’s Dark Side of the Moon.

questions.q: What’s a trait you value in creative people?
questions.a: Those who are willing to try an idea out even if it sounds ridiculous to them.

questions.q: What’s something you think people take too seriously?
questions.a: The never ending battle between analog vs digital, plugins vs gear, real amps vs amp sims. Who cares…
